title: Drawknife-shaved ash rake handle
subtitle: A replacement or first-time rake handle, shaped by hand
excerpt: A garden rake handle in green ash: riven from a straight section of timber, shaved to a 32 mm round taper on the shaving horse, and dried before fitting. Green ash for the shaving, seasoned ash for the tenon end. A practical first project on the shaving horse.

glossaryTerms.definition: Freshly felled or recently riven wood, still high in moisture content. Carves easily under hand tools.
A foot-operated clamp bench for holding work while using a drawknife or spokeshave.
Splitting wood along the grain using a froe and mallet rather than sawing across it. Riven surfaces follow the grain and are stronger than sawn surfaces.

content.text: A rake handle is a long, straight pole, round in cross-section, tapering very slightly from handle-grip to the rake-head socket. At 1.5 m and 32 mm diameter it looks simple, but the required straightness and even taper make it a good discipline project on the
shaving horse
. This project uses
green wood

ash because the green state shaves fast and ash dries straight without significant movement. Beginner level for shaving-horse work, though a straight eye and patience with the long blank are required.
Before you start.
Drawknife: the drawknife is pulled toward the body. Control the bevel angle and the stopping point. Never allow the blade to travel past the thigh.
Shaving horse: the foot pedal must lock the work before the drawknife stroke begins.
First aid: keep a styptic pencil, gauze, and a clean dressing within reach. Apply firm pressure, elevate, and dress. A cut that shows fat or won't close with pressure goes to A&E, not a plaster.
Wood
A 1.6 m section of straight ash, diameter 50 to 60 mm. This can come from a larger branch, from
riving

a section of trunk (with froe and beetle), or from a timber merchant's ash round in the green state. Hazel is an alternative for a lighter handle: hazel poles of the right diameter are common coppice material and shave very quickly. Avoid sap-stained or checked sections.
Method
Step 1: Rough the blank to octagonal

Mount the blank in the shaving horse. Use the drawknife bevel-up to take long sweeping strokes along the blank, removing the bulk of the round section and leaving an approximate octagonal cross-section. Work from the thick end toward the thin end, with the grain.
Step 2: Shave to round

Take the octagonal section to a round by shaving the eight edges. Rotate the blank in the shaving horse clamp to access each face. Check the diameter with a caliper every 20 cm along the length. Target diameter is 32 to 34 mm at the grip end, 26 to 28 mm at the rake head end.
Step 3: Spokeshave the finish

The optional round spokeshave gives a smoother, more consistent surface than the drawknife alone. Mount the blank in the horse and work the spokeshave in the same direction as the drawknife strokes. The spokeshave removes a thinner shaving and is used for the final 2 mm of diameter reduction.
Step 4: Dry the handle

Hang the handle horizontally for six to eight weeks in a ventilated shed. Check for curl every two weeks. If curl develops, tie the handle to a straight batten until dry. Do not force the drying with a heater.
Finishing and fitting

Once dry, apply raw linseed oil to all surfaces. One coat, left one hour, wiped surplus. Cure for two weeks before fitting to the rake head. The rake-head end is tapered slightly to fit the socket, which may require a further light pass with the drawknife after drying to achieve the correct fit diameter. The cure time is the same for the handle as for any other raw-linseed piece.

attrs.symptom: The handle has a flat section near the middle
attrs.cause: The shaving horse clamp left a compression mark where the blank was gripped.
attrs.fix: Release the clamp and reposition so the mark is not under the clamp foot. Shave the flat section lightly to blend it back to round.

attrs.symptom: The handle is not straight after drying
attrs.cause: The blank had inherent tension from a curved growth position.
attrs.fix: Tie to a straight batten with cotton tape and re-check after two weeks. Most ash handles straighten fully within three weeks of being tied.
